result.text:
401: \end{align*}
402: The endpoint distance depends only on the two metrics, whereas
403: $\mathcal D(\bV)$ depends on the selected path.  The direct SPD path length is
404: independent of a factorization; the upper bound from
405: \Cref{lem:factor-spd-path} depends on the chosen factorization and interpolation.
406: \end{remark}
407: 
408: \begin{remark}[Sharpness of the symmetric exponential factors]
409: For $D\ge0$, let
410: \[
411: \begin{aligned}
412:  \bVbar&=\bI_2,&
413:  \bV&=\begin{pmatrix}e^D&0\\0&e^{-D}\end{pmatrix},\\
414:  \bV(\tau)&=\begin{pmatrix}e^{D\tau}&0\\0&e^{-D\tau}\end{pmatrix}.
415: \end{aligned}
416: \]
417: Then
418: \[
419:  \bV(\tau)^{-1/2}\dot\bV(\tau)\bV(\tau)^{-1/2}
420:  =\begin{pmatrix}D&0\\0&-D\end{pmatrix},
421: \]
422: so $\mathcal D(\bV)=d_{\rm Th}(\bVbar,\bV)=D$.  For $q_1=e_1$,
423: $\bar s(q_1)=1$ and $s(q_1)=e^{-D/2}$, so
424: $\bar s=e^{D/2}s$ is attained.  For $q_2=e_2$,
425: $s(q_2)=e^{D/2}$ and $\bar s(q_2)=1$, so
426: $s=e^{D/2}\bar s$ is attained.  Thus each one-way factor is sharp, and a
427: uniform argument based only on the symmetric Thompson-distance bound cannot
428: improve the resulting round-trip factor $e^D$.  This is a metric-factor
429: sharpness statement, not a contextual-bandit regret lower bound and not a
430: claim that every trajectory attains the worst case.
431: \end{remark}
432: 
433: \begin{lemma}[Rectangular factor-path certificate]
434: \label{lem:factor-spd-path}
435: Let $\Bmat:[0,1]\to\R^{m\times d}$ be absolutely continuous and set
436: $\bV(\tau)=\lambda\bI+\Bmat(\tau)^\top\Bmat(\tau)$, with $\lambda>0$.
437: Then
438: \begin{equation}\label{eq:factor-path-bound-new}
439:  \mathcal D(\bV)\le2\int_0^1
440:  \|\dot\Bmat(\tau)\bV(\tau)^{-1/2}\|_{\rm op}\,d\tau.
441: \end{equation}
442: More generally, suppose there is a measurable function
443: $\nu_t:[0,1]\to[0,\infty)$ with $\nu_t\in L^1([0,1])$ such that
444: \[
445:  \dot\Bmat(\tau)^\top\dot\Bmat(\tau)
446:  \preceq\nu_t(\tau)^2\bV(\tau)
447: \]
448: almost everywhere.  Then
449: $\mathcal D(\bV)\le2\int_0^1\nu_t(\tau)d\tau$.  For nonnegative $\nu_t$, the
450: displayed PSD premise is equivalently the norm condition
451: $\|\dot\Bmat(\tau)\bV(\tau)^{-1/2}\|_{\rm op}\le\nu_t(\tau)$ almost everywhere.
452: \end{lemma}
453: 
454: For scalar differentiable means, take the $s$th row of $\Bmat_t(\tau)$ to be
455: \begin{equation}\label{eq:scalar-factor-path-new}
456:  \sigma^{-1}\nabla_\theta\mu_{\btheta_s+
457:  \tau(\btheta_t-\btheta_s)}(x_s,a_s)^\top.
458: \end{equation}
459: This interpolates from collection-time frozen curvature to the exact current
460: relinearized curvature.  It is a synthetic path in stacked factor space: each
461: replay factor follows its own segment from the collection-time Jacobian to the
462: current relinearized Jacobian.  The stacked path need not equal the GGN evaluated
463: at one common intermediate parameter shared by all replay samples.
464: A weighted or heteroscedastic squared loss uses row
465: $\sqrt{w_s}\,\nabla\mu^\top$ for a nonnegative collection-time weight $w_s$
466: fixed before the corresponding reward.
467: If the weight is fixed along the interpolation, the same proof only rescales
468: the corresponding row.  If it changes with the path, the derivative of
469: $\sqrt{w_s(\tau)}$ is an additional obligation.
470: 
471: \begin{corollary}[Hessian path certificate]
472: \label{cor:hessian-path-new}
473: Suppose the parameter region is convex and
474: $\|\nabla_\theta^2\mu_\theta(x_s,a_s)\|_{\rm op}\le L_g$ along every segment
475: in \eqref{eq:scalar-factor-path-new}.  With
476: \begin{equation}\label{eq:Qt-new}
477:  Q_t=\sum_{s<t}\|\btheta_t-\btheta_s\|_2^2,
478: \end{equation}
479: the exact current and frozen metrics satisfy
480: \begin{equation}\label{eq:hessian-path-sandwich-new}
481:  e^{-\bar D_t}\bVbar_t\preceq\bV_t\preceq e^{\bar D_t}\bVbar_t,
482:  \qquad
483:  \bar D_t=\frac{2L_g\sqrt{Q_t}}{\sigma\sqrt\lambda}.
484: \end{equation}
485: This remains valid when $\bar D_t\ge1$.  At $t=1$, the factor has zero rows,
486: $Q_1=0$, and both metrics equal $\lambda\bI$.
487: \end{corollary}
488: 
489: The relative condition in \Cref{lem:factor-spd-path} can be much sharper than
490: the ridge-only bound in \Cref{cor:hessian-path-new}: excitation in the current
491: metric attenuates motion in already-observed directions.  It permits arbitrary
492: gradient rotation and requires neither a fixed subspace nor known rank.
493: 
494: \begin{proposition}[Width transport and approximate operators]
495: \label{prop:width-transport-new}
496: Under \eqref{eq:path-length-new} and \eqref{eq:operator-sandwich-new},
497: \begin{align}
498:  \bar s_t^2(a)&\le e^{\bar D_t}\kappa_{+,t}s_{\Calg,t}^2(a),
499:  &s_{\Calg,t}^2(a)&\le
500:  e^{\bar D_t}\kappa_{-,t}^{-1}\bar s_t^2(a).
501:  \label{eq:two-way-width-new}
502: \end{align}
503: Exact current curvature has $\kappa_{-,t}=\kappa_{+,t}=1$.  More generally,
504: the operational relative-error certificate
505: \begin{equation}\label{eq:relative-operator-certificate-new}
506:  \|\bV_t^{-1/2}(\Calg_t-\bV_t)\bV_t^{-1/2}\|_{\rm op}
507:  \le\varepsilon_t<1
508: \end{equation}
509: gives $\kappa_{-,t}=1-\varepsilon_t$ and
510: $\kappa_{+,t}=1+\varepsilon_t$.  An upper comparison alone does not imply a
511: lower factor.
512: \end{proposition}
513: 
514: \begin{corollary}[Direct endpoint sandwich]
515: \label{cor:relative-endpoint-ucb}
516: Replace the path premise \eqref{eq:path-length-new} in
517: \Cref{thm:transported-ucb} by pre-reward measurable factors that, on the joint
518: certificate event, satisfy
519: \begin{equation}\label{eq:relative-endpoint-sandwich}
520:  0<c_{-,t}\le c_{+,t}<\infty,\qquad
521:  c_{-,t}\bVbar_t\preceq\bV_t\preceq c_{+,t}\bVbar_t.
522: \end{equation}
523: Replace \eqref{eq:transported-score-new} by the score
524: \begin{equation}\label{eq:relative-endpoint-score}
525:  U_t^{\rm rel}(a)=m_t(a)+\beta_t\sqrt{c_{+,t}\kappa_{+,t}}
526:  \hat s_t(a)+b_t(a),
527: \end{equation}
528: and require the same finite measurable supremum and approximate-selector
529: condition for this score.  Keep every other hypothesis of that theorem.
530: On the joint confidence and certificate event, writing
531: $h_t=1+\alpha_t\sqrt{c_{+,t}\kappa_{+,t}/(c_{-,t}\kappa_{-,t})}$,
532: \begin{align}
533:  \operatorname{reg}_t
534:  &\le\beta_t h_t\bar s_t(a_t)+2b_t(a_t)+\xi_t,\nonumber\\
535:  R_T&\le\sqrt{\left(\sigma^2+\frac{G^2}{\lambda}\right)
536:  \gamma_T\sum_{t=1}^T\beta_t^2h_t^2}
537:  +2\sum_{t=1}^Tb_t(a_t)+\sum_{t=1}^T\xi_t.
538:  \label{eq:relative-endpoint-regret}
539: \end{align}
540: The probability statement of \Cref{thm:transported-ucb} is unchanged, with
541: the endpoint certificate included in its joint certificate event.
542: \end{corollary}
543: 
544: This result uses the endpoint matrices directly.  In particular,
545: $\max\{-\log c_{-,t},\log c_{+,t}\}$ bounds their Thompson distance;
546: it need not bound the length of the synthetic path
547: \eqref{eq:scalar-factor-path-new}.  Its effective width still obeys the
548: reference-width floor: $\sqrt{c_{+,t}\kappa_{+,t}}\hat s_t(a)\ge\bar s_t(a)$.
549: 
550: For vector outputs, let $J_s(\theta)\in\R^{p_s\times d}$ and supply an
551: absolutely continuous factor $R_s(\theta)\in\R^{r_s\times p_s}$ satisfying
552: $R_s^\top R_s=W_s\succeq0$.  Stacking
553: $B_s=R_sJ_s\in\R^{r_s\times d}$ gives
554: $\lambda I+\sum_sJ_s^\top W_sJ_s$.  Along a path,
555: $\dot B_s=\dot R_sJ_s+R_s\dot J_s$; both terms must be controlled.  This
556: covers the geometry of weighted Fisher/GGN factors but does not by itself prove
557: a likelihood confidence sequence or an exponential-family regret theorem.

559: \section{Corrected-center squared-loss specialization}
560: \label{sec:corrected-center}
561: 
562: We next instantiate the reference-confidence interface.  The corrected center
563: keeps statistical estimation in the predictable collection-time features while
564: using the current nonlinear prediction as its anchor.  The resulting identity
565: does not assume that the representation parameter minimizes a nonlinear loss.
566: Let $\sigma>0$ and let
567: the reward obey $r_t=\mu_t^*(a_t)+\eta_t$, where, for every $u\in\R$,
568: \begin{equation}\label{eq:new-noise-condition}
569:  \mathbb E[\exp(u\eta_t)\mid\cHist_t]
570:  \le\exp(u^2\sigma^2/2).
571: \end{equation}
572: Thus the noise condition is imposed after the action is selected and before
573: the reward is revealed.  The ridge penalty is centered at zero in the chosen
574: parameter coordinates, and every norm bound below, including
575: $\|\btheta^\circ\|_2\le S$, uses those coordinates.  For a pretrained
576: initialization $\btheta_0$, the intended convention is displacement coordinates
577: $\btheta=\btheta_{\rm orig}-\btheta_0$; then $S$ bounds the displacement of the
578: reference model from initialization rather than its raw parameter norm.  Fix
579: before data collection a reference parameter $\btheta^\circ\in\Theta$ with
580: $\|\btheta^\circ\|_2\le S$, and allow
581: approximate realizability
582: \begin{equation}\label{eq:approx-realizability-new}
583:  \mu^*(z)=\mu_{\btheta^\circ}(z)+m^\circ(z),\qquad
584:  |m^\circ(z)|\le\epsilon_{\rm mis}(z).
585: \end{equation}
586: The predictable sequence $\btheta_t\in\Theta$ is otherwise arbitrary.  Set
587: $\bq_t(a)=\nabla_\theta\mu_{\btheta_t}(x_t,a)$ and define collection-time
588: pseudo-responses and the frozen ridge estimator by
589: \begin{align}
590:  y_s&=r_s-\mu_{\btheta_s}(x_s,a_s)+\bq_s(a_s)^\top\btheta_s,
591:  \label{eq:pseudo-response-new}\\
592:  \hat\btheta_t^{\rm lin}
593:  &=\bVbar_t^{-1}\sigma^{-2}\sum_{s<t}\bq_s(a_s)y_s.
594:  \label{eq:frozen-ridge-new}
595: \end{align}
596: The corrected center is
597: \begin{equation}\label{eq:corrected-center-new}
598:  m_t^{\rm corr}(a)=\mu_{\btheta_t}(x_t,a)
599:  +\bq_t(a)^\top(\hat\btheta_t^{\rm lin}-\btheta_t).
600: \end{equation}
601: 
602: Fix $\delta\in(0,1)$.  Let $\rho_s^\circ$ be the Taylor remainder of
603: $\mu_{\btheta^\circ}$ around $\btheta_s$, and supply envelopes
604: \begin{equation}\label{eq:lin-mis-envelopes-new}
605:  |\rho_s^\circ|\le\epsilon_{\rm lin}(s),\qquad
606:  |m^\circ(x_s,a_s)|\le\epsilon_{\rm mis}(s),
607: \end{equation}
608: with the corresponding actionwise current envelopes
609: $\epsilon_{\rm lin,t}(a)$ and $\epsilon_{\rm mis,t}(a)$.  Each envelope is
610: deterministic or measurable before the reward at the round where it is used;
611: the complete historical sum below is known before selecting $a_t$.  Define
612: \begin{equation}\label{eq:beta-corrected-new}
613:  \begin{aligned}
614:   \beta_t^{\rm corr}
615:   &=\sqrt{\gamma_{t-1}+2\log(1/\delta)}+\sqrt\lambda S\\
616:   &\quad+\frac1\sigma\sqrt{\sum_{s<t}
617:   [\epsilon_{\rm lin}(s)+\epsilon_{\rm mis}(s)]^2}.
618:  \end{aligned}
619: \end{equation}
620: 
621: \begin{corollary}[Corrected-center confidence without optimizer assumptions]
622: \label{cor:corrected-center-new}
623: With probability at least $1-\delta$, simultaneously over rounds and actions,
624: \begin{equation}\label{eq:corrected-confidence-new}
625:  |\mu_t^*(a)-m_t^{\rm corr}(a)|
626:  \le\beta_t^{\rm corr}\bar s_t(a)
627:  +\epsilon_{\rm lin,t}(a)+\epsilon_{\rm mis,t}(a).
628: \end{equation}
629: The identity and bound hold for any predictable $\btheta_t$ in the certified
630: region.  They require no exact ERM, approximate stationarity, optimizer
631: residual, or optimizer convergence rate.
632: \end{corollary}
633: 
634: The historical deterministic term in \eqref{eq:beta-corrected-new} follows from
635: $\Phi_t^\top\bVbar_t^{-1}\Phi_t\preceq I$ for
636: $\Phi_t=[\bq_1/\sigma,\ldots,\bq_{t-1}/\sigma]$.  Its scaling is
637: $1/\sigma$, not $1/\sigma^2$.  Fixed nonvanishing misspecification generally
638: creates a linear current-bias term and can also make the historical radius
639: vacuous.  This is a graceful-degradation statement, not a robust
640: misspecified-bandit guarantee.
641: 
642: \section{Closed finite-dimensional rates and local alternatives}
643: \label{sec:closed-rates-new}
644: 
645: Let $r_T=\min\{d,T\}$.  Rank--trace concavity gives the primitive closure
646: \begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-d-gamma-new}
647:  \gamma_T\le\Gamma_{T,d}:=
648:  r_T\log\!\left(1+\frac{TG^2}{r_T\lambda\sigma^2}\right).
649: \end{equation}
650: No fixed tangent subspace is required.
651: 
652: \begin{corollary}[Finite-dimensional corrected-center rate]
653: \label{cor:finite-d-rate-new}
654: Suppose $\bar D_t\le D$, $\alpha_t\le\alpha$, and
655: $\kappa_{+,t}/\kappa_{-,t}\le K$ for all $t$.  Let
656: \begin{align*}
657:  B_T&=\sum_{s<T}[\epsilon_{\rm lin}(s)+\epsilon_{\rm mis}(s)]^2,\\
658:  E_T^{\rm cur}&=\sum_{t=1}^T
659:  [\epsilon_{\rm lin,t}(a_t)+\epsilon_{\rm mis,t}(a_t)].
660: \end{align*}
661: Then \Cref{thm:transported-ucb,cor:corrected-center-new} imply
662: \begin{align}
663: R_T
664: &\le2\alpha e^D\sqrt K\nonumber\\
665: &\quad{}\times
666: \left[\sqrt{\Gamma_{T,d}+2\log(1/\delta)}+\sqrt\lambda S
667: +\frac{\sqrt{B_T}}{\sigma}\right]\nonumber\\
668: &\quad{}\times
669: \sqrt{\left(\sigma^2+\frac{G^2}{\lambda}\right)T\Gamma_{T,d}}
670: \nonumber\\
671: &\quad+2E_T^{\rm cur}+\sum_{t=1}^T\xi_t.
672: \label{eq:finite-d-rate-new-display}
673: \end{align}
674: With exact realizability and a frozen linear model, $B_T=E_T^{\rm cur}=0$.
675: For fixed $d$ and problem constants, the leading term is then
676: $O(e^D\sqrt K\,d\sqrt T\log T)$.  Exact solves set $\alpha=1$, exact current
677: curvature sets $K=1$, and exact score maximization sets $\xi_t=0$, recovering
678: the standard LinUCB determinant-potential rate up to displayed constants.
679: \end{corollary}
680: 
681: \begin{corollary}[Global near-linearity under exponential transport]
682: \label{cor:global-near-linear-new}
683: Assume exact realizability, $\mu^*(z)=\mu_{\btheta^\circ}(z)$, and suppose
684: $\|\btheta^\circ\|_2\le R$ and $\|\btheta_t\|_2\le R$ for every $t$.
685: On the certified convex radius-$R$ region, assume the prediction gradient is
686: $L_\mu$-Lipschitz for the Taylor envelopes and satisfies the replay-path
687: Hessian bound $L_g$ in \Cref{cor:hessian-path-new}, with
688: \[
689:  L_\mu\le\frac{c_\mu}{\sqrt W},\qquad
690:  L_g\le\frac{c_g}{\sqrt W},
691: \]
692: with $W>0$.  Use the corrected center, exact current curvature, exact dense
693: solves, and exact score maximization in finite parameter dimension $d$, and
694: suppose $\|\bq_t(a)\|_2\le G$.  Thus
695: $\alpha_t=1$, $\kappa_{-,t}=\kappa_{+,t}=1$, and $\xi_t=0$.
696: Define
697: \[
698:  D_{T,W}:=\frac{4c_gR\sqrt{T-1}}{\sigma\sqrt{\lambda W}}.
699: \]
700: Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$,
701: \begin{align}
702:  R_T
703:  &\le 2e^{D_{T,W}}
704:  \Biggl[
705:  \begin{aligned}
706:   &\sqrt{\Gamma_{T,d}+2\log(1/\delta)}+\sqrt\lambda R\\[-1mm]
707:   &\quad+\frac{2c_\mu R^2\sqrt T}{\sigma\sqrt W}
708:  \end{aligned}
709:  \Biggr]\nonumber\\[-1mm]
710:  &\quad\times
711:  \sqrt{\sigma^2+\frac{G^2}{\lambda}}\,
712:  \sqrt{T\Gamma_{T,d}}\nonumber\\
713:  &\quad+\frac{4c_\mu R^2T}{\sqrt W}.
714:  \label{eq:global-near-linear-new}
715: \end{align}
716: Consequently, $W=\Omega(T)$ with a sufficiently large problem-dependent
717: constant keeps $D_{T,W}=O(1)$.  For fixed $d$ and fixed problem constants,
718: \[
719:  R_T=O(d\sqrt T\log T)+O(\sqrt T).
720: \]
721: This conclusion requires no $D_t<1$ condition.  Here $W$ is an abstract
722: near-linearity scale, not generic network width or parameter count, and the
723: result is not an unrestricted neural-training theorem.  No optimizer-residual
724: rate is required because the corrected center is used.
725: \end{corollary}
726: 
727: \begin{remark}[Comparable guarantees do not order policies]
728: \Cref{prop:frozen-width-ucb,cor:corrected-center-new} give a frozen-width
729: counterpart to \eqref{eq:finite-d-rate-new-display}, with the factor
730: $\alpha e^D\sqrt K$ removed and all remaining quantities evaluated on the
731: frozen policy's own history.  With the same $\lambda$, $\sigma$, and
732: confidence level, common uniform bounds on the query norm, reference norm,
733: approximation envelopes, and accumulated oracle error give guarantees of the
734: same order when $D$, $\alpha$, and $K$ are bounded.  In particular, under the
735: statistical, uniform-region, and smoothness assumptions of
736: \Cref{cor:global-near-linear-new}, the corrected center and exact
737: frozen-width score maximization give the same
738: $O(d\sqrt T\log T)+O(\sqrt T)$ rate when $W=\Omega(T)$, for fixed $d$
739: and fixed problem constants.
740: This comparison does not rank realized regret: different selected actions
741: change the representation paths, centers, radii, and information gains.
742: It neither proves that transport is unnecessary nor rules out improved
743: performance from current curvature.  The stated $W$ scaling is a sufficient
744: condition for these bounds, not a necessary condition for an informative
745: transport certificate.
746: \end{remark}
747: 
748: \begin{remark}[Scaled-tanh specialization]
749: For
750: \[
751:  \mu_{\btheta,W}(z)=\sqrt W\tanh\!\left(
752:  \frac{\phi(z)^\top\btheta}{\sqrt W}\right),
753:  \qquad \|\phi(z)\|_2\le B_\phi,
754: \]
755: write $u=\phi(z)^\top\btheta/\sqrt W$.  Then
756: \begin{align*}
757:  \nabla_\theta\mu_{\btheta,W}(z)
758:  &=\operatorname{sech}^2(u)\phi(z),\\
759:  \nabla_\theta^2\mu_{\btheta,W}(z)
760:  &=-\frac{2}{\sqrt W}\operatorname{sech}^2(u)\tanh(u)
761:  \phi(z)\phi(z)^\top.
762: \end{align*}
763: Since
764: $\sup_u|2\operatorname{sech}^2(u)\tanh(u)|=4/(3\sqrt3)$,
765: \Cref{cor:global-near-linear-new} applies with
766: \[
767:  G=B_\phi,\qquad
768:  c_\mu=c_g=c_h:=\frac{4B_\phi^2}{3\sqrt3}.
769: \]
770: The symbol $W$ is a smoothness scale here; it is not identified with hidden
771: width or parameter count.
772: \end{remark}
773: 
774: \begin{corollary}[Relative weights for scaled tanh]
775: \label{cor:tanh-relative-weights}
776: For the scaled-tanh model above, suppose $W>0$, $\|\phi(z_s)\|_2\le B_\phi$,
777: and $\|\btheta_s\|_2,\|\btheta_t\|_2\le R$ for all $s<t$.
778: Set $\omega_\theta(z)=\operatorname{sech}^2(\phi(z)^\top\theta/\sqrt W)$ and
779: $\ell=\operatorname{sech}^2(B_\phi R/\sqrt W)>0$.  For
780: \begin{align*}
781:  \bVbar_t&=\lambda\bI+\sigma^{-2}\sum_{s<t}
782:  \omega_{\btheta_s}(z_s)^2\phi(z_s)\phi(z_s)^\top,\\
783:  \bV_t&=\lambda\bI+\sigma^{-2}\sum_{s<t}
784:  \omega_{\btheta_t}(z_s)^2\phi(z_s)\phi(z_s)^\top,
785: \end{align*}
786: the uniform endpoint certificate is
787: \begin{equation}\label{eq:tanh-uniform-relative}
788:  \ell^2\bVbar_t\preceq\bV_t\preceq\ell^{-2}\bVbar_t,
789:  \qquad d_{\rm Th}(\bVbar_t,\bV_t)
790:  \le4\log\cosh(B_\phi R/\sqrt W).
791: \end{equation}
792: If the observed feature vectors belong to a finite set $\{\phi_c\}$, let
793: $n_{t,c}$ be their counts, let
794: $f_{t,c}=\sum_{s<t:\phi(z_s)=\phi_c}\omega_{\btheta_s}(z_s)^2$, and put
795: $g_{t,c}=n_{t,c}\operatorname{sech}^4(\phi_c^\top\btheta_t/\sqrt W)$.
796: The sharper category certificate is
797: \begin{equation}\label{eq:tanh-category-relative}
798:  c_{-,t}=\min\!\left\{1,\min_{c:n_{t,c}>0}\frac{g_{t,c}}{f_{t,c}}\right\},
799:  \qquad
800:  c_{+,t}=\max\!\left\{1,\max_{c:n_{t,c}>0}\frac{g_{t,c}}{f_{t,c}}\right\},
